title: Demo environment enablement: training agenda + certification rubric (v1)
body:
Context
- Goal: Every AE/SE runs a consistent, reliable Redwood demo (30 min standard) using the demo tenant, with a known-good set of scenarios and a safe backup path.
- This plan covers training sessions + a lightweight certification so we can (a) raise baseline quality, (b) reduce demo failures, (c) keep messaging consistent across NA/EMEA.

Audience / who should attend
- Required: All Sales Engineers (SE team), all AEs who run their own live API clicks (Avery/Priyom/Hannah pilot group first).
- Recommended: CSMs who support POCs, PMM (for messaging consistency), SRE on-call shadow (first cohort only).

Success criteria (for enablement rollout)
- 90%+ of live demos run using the new demo tenant within 2 weeks of training.
- Reset time: <10 minutes median (measured by SE self-report for now; automation metrics later).
- Demo failure rate (needs backup mode): <10% of demos.
- Everyone certified can execute: (1) core API live flow, (2) economics toggles + explain, (3) fallback story + show, (4) console tour without empty dashboards.

Definitions (so we’re aligned)
- "Demo tenant": Redwood-controlled, production-like tenant with pinned models/versions, seeded projects/keys, seeded usage + synthetic traffic so Console looks real.
- "Known-good scenario": A scripted flow with expected outcomes and a regression definition (what counts as broken).
- "Backup mode": A prepared fallback path (screenshots/recording/canned outputs) that preserves narrative if live steps fail.

Training delivery plan (cohorts)
- Cohort 1 (pilot): SE leads + AE pilot users (Avery, Priyom, Hannah). Target: week of 2025-11-25.
- Cohort 2 (all field): All AEs + SEs. Target: early Dec.
- Cohort 3 (EMEA variant): EMEA-focused emphasis on residency/private narrative. Target: mid Dec.

Schedule + agenda (90 minutes live + 30 minutes self-serve)

Session 1: "Demo in 30" (90 min, instructor-led)
Owner: Markus Klein (technical) + Soojin Lee (messaging)

0. Pre-reads (self-serve, 30 min)
- Demo deck (v1) skim: focus on slide order and the 3 main story beats.
- Talk track script: read the transitions + discovery questions.
- Runbook quick glance: reset + healthcheck sections.

1. Intro (5 min)
- Why we’re standardizing: reliability, repeatability, and consistent claims.
- What changed: demo tenant, pinned routes, synthetic dashboards, single reset workflow.

2. Narrative + positioning (15 min)
- Story arc: "Production economics" + "Unified inference across hosted/dedicated/private" + "Reliability via graceful degradation".
- How to tailor quickly: Hosted-first vs Dedicated-first vs Private/security-first.
- What NOT to say: avoid implying Dedicated = single-tenant metal unless that’s true; do not over-promise private deployment timelines.

3. Live run-of-show walkthrough (30 min)
- Steps (SE leads, AEs watch for language + pacing):
  a) Core API demo: streaming chat completion → structured output → tool calling.
  b) Economics demo: show cost/latency breakdown and toggle batching/caching presets.
  c) Reliability demo: show fallback policy concept + demonstrate a controlled fallback (if enabled in demo routes).
  d) Observability demo: show token-level cost, error analysis, traces, rollout view (if stable).
- Timing guidance:
  - Core API: 10–12 min
  - Economics: 6–8 min
  - Reliability: 4–5 min
  - Console tour: 6–8 min
  - Q&A buffer: 3–5 min

4. Demo tenant operations (15 min)
- Access model: least-privilege keys; no key sharing in Slack; short-lived creds where available.
- Reset flow (what to do before every demo):
  - Run reset + healthcheck command (or internal tool)
  - Validate dashboards are populated (synthetic traffic running)
  - Confirm model pin + fallback policy status
- How to handle parallel demos: use assigned project namespace + separate scoped key.

5. Failure modes + backup mode (10 min)
- If dashboards are empty: run synthetic traffic job / switch to backup screenshots.
- If 429 throttling: reduce concurrency; check quota; switch to canned outputs for economics section.
- If streaming flakes: switch to non-streaming response; narrate what streaming would show.
- If auth/RBAC breaks: do not "borrow" someone else’s key; use the escalation path and backup mode.

6. Certification overview + next steps (5 min)
- What is required to be certified.
- Deadlines.
- Where to find assets.

Session 2: "Hands-on lab" (60 min, small groups)
Owner: Renee Sullivan + Alex Martinez
- Everyone runs the full scripted scenario themselves.
- We intentionally trigger one failure mode per participant (assigned) and practice backup path.
- Quick peer feedback on pacing + talk track.

Session 3 (optional): Enterprise/security module (45 min)
Owner: Simran Kaur + Naomi Feldman
- What security reviewers care about (SSO/SAML, audit logs, retention/residency, encryption/KMS).
- Safe sharing rules for screenshots and logs.
- How to answer "Private" questions without over-committing.

Certification rubric (v1)

Certification levels
- Level 1: "Core Demo Certified" (required for SEs and any AE who runs a live demo solo)
- Level 2: "Advanced / Enterprise Certified" (recommended for enterprise SEs + AEs handling security-first cycles)

Who evaluates
- Primary: Markus Klein (SE lead) or delegated SE manager.
- Messaging spot-check: Soojin Lee (PMM) for first 5 certs per region.
- Operations spot-check: Sean Gallagher (SRE) for random sampling (demo readiness, escalation compliance).

Core Demo Certified (Level 1) — requirements
Candidate must demonstrate, in a dry-run:
A) Pre-demo readiness (PASS/FAIL)
- Can run reset + healthcheck successfully and interpret results.
- Confirms keys are scoped correctly and stored appropriately.
- Confirms dashboards show data (or proactively opens backup screenshots).

B) Live demo execution (scored 0–2 each; minimum total score required)
Scoring: 0 = missed/broken, 1 = partial, 2 = complete and well-explained.

1) Discovery + setup (0–2)
- Asks 2–3 relevant discovery questions (use case + constraints + success metric).
- Selects the right narrative branch (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

2) Core API scenario (0–2)
- Demonstrates streaming response.
- Shows structured output / JSON schema style response.
- Demonstrates tool calling (or a clear simulation) and explains retry behavior.

3) Economics + unit cost story (0–2)
- Shows token-level cost/latency breakdown.
- Explains batching/caching levers as "controls" not magic.
- Avoids unapproved benchmark claims; states caveats correctly.

4) Reliability / graceful degradation (0–2)
- Explains pinned model/version concept.
- Explains allowed fallback policy (model family/region) and why it reduces incidents.
- Demonstrates fallback (if available) OR uses backup artifacts while keeping credibility.

5) Console tour / observability (0–2)
- Navigates to: request traces (or equivalent), errors view, cost view, rollout/canary view (only if stable).
- Explains how to operationalize (alerts, regression detection) at a high level.

6) Handling one injected failure mode (0–2)
Evaluator picks ONE:
- Empty dashboard
- 429 throttling
- Streaming disconnect
- Model unavailable / fallback path
- Auth/RBAC failure (simulate)
Candidate must:
- Stay calm, keep narrative moving.
- Switch to backup mode within 60–90 seconds.
- State what happened without blaming the customer.

C) Security + data handling (PASS/FAIL)
- Clearly states demo data is synthetic (no customer data).
- Uses safe-sharing practices (no secrets on screen, no copy/paste keys).
- Knows where to find Security FAQ links.

Passing thresholds (Level 1)
- PASS all PASS/FAIL items (A and C)
- Score >= 10/12 across the six scored categories (B)
- No single scored category can be 0

Advanced / Enterprise Certified (Level 2) — additions
Candidate can:
- Explain Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options without over-claiming.
- Answer common enterprise objections:
  - Data retention/residency
  - SSO/SAML + RBAC
  - Audit logs
  - SLA and uptime expectations (demo vs prod)
- Demonstrate (or narrate with screenshots) VPC/Private architecture and controls.
- Run a "reliability objection" branch: what happens when capacity is constrained.

Fail / remediation plan
- If not passed: evaluator provides a short punch list (max 5 items) and assigns a re-test within 7–10 days.
- If repeated failure: candidate shadows 2 certified demos and repeats hands-on lab.

Certification logistics
- Sign-up: calendared slots (30 min per candidate) + one 60 min buffer per cohort for overruns.
- Recording: internal only; store in shared drive folder "demo-environment/certification-recordings" (no customer names).
- Tracking: Elliot to maintain a simple roster (Name, Region, Level, Date, Evaluator, Notes).

Asset list (what every certified person should have bookmarked)
- Demo deck v1 + backup deck PDF (if available)
- Talk track script v1
- Run-of-show (30 min standard)
- Demo scenario checklist (pre-flight)
- Demo tenant reset runbook + healthcheck
- Demo failure modes + backup plan
- Security FAQ links + safe-sharing rules

Owners
